_readme: DECLARED COUNTS (checked by test/corpus_independence_test.dart, which reads them from tools/ai_accuracy.py --corpus and fails if they go stale): 31 cases over 26 distinct dish families; 22 distinct dish CLASSES; 38 coverage classes; top-4 classes hold 42%. ROADMAP M1 bar = 20 MEALS = 20 distinct dish classes. MET at 21, with one class to spare.
Labelled truth for tools/ai_accuracy.py.
Batch 1: 5 openly licensed, human-reviewed Indian meals plus the 1 original in-repo photo and 1 out-of-scope probe.
RoADMAP M1 asks for 20. We are not there yet, and the count is not
the thing being optimised - a corpus of 5 photos of the same dish
would score beautifully and tell us nothing.
kcal values are IFCT-style REFERENCE figures for the visible portion,
not laboratory measurements. 'confidence' is my honest read of how
defensible the label is: a thali I can name item by item is 'high'; a
bowl that a scan could fairly call either kadhi or dal is 'medium'.
Anything I could not name honestly was deleted, not guessed at.
Batch 2 added 5 more openly licensed, human-reviewed meals, chosen for dish BREADTH: 8 of the 16 candidates were bhindi, exactly the trap batch 1 hit with chole bhature, so only one bhindi was taken.

Batch 3 added 5 more openly licensed, human-reviewed meals. THE TRAP, THIRD TIME: of 18 candidates 8 were masala dosa and 7 were idli, so only 5 distinct dishes were taken. THE HONEST LIMIT: because the queries were breakfast items, all five are South-Indian breakfast. That is a real bias in the corpus; batch 4 must target curries, eggs and non-breakfast home cooking before any overall score is quoted.

Batch 4 added 5 more human-reviewed, non-breakfast meals. THE TRAP, FOURTH TIME: of 20 candidates 14 were chana/chole/chole-bhature, because three search terms were chole-based. Three of the five kept are therefore the same legume family - recorded here rather than hidden. Batch 5 must search one dish at a time to escape it. Batch 4 also adds the corpus's only NON-VEGETARIAN case, which was a real gap: our users are not all vegetarian and nothing else tested that.
INDEPENDENCE (2026-09-28). "22 cases" is NOT 22 facts. Three dish families
repeat here, so their errors carry 3x the weight of a family that appears once:
dal x3 (thali_ma08, chapati_dal_bhindi_plate, non_veg_thali),
chole x3 (north_indian_dinner, chole_papad_plate, chole_puri_halwa_thali),
sambar x2 (idli_sambar_chutney_plate, tamil_uthappam).
So: 22 cases over 17 DISTINCT dish families; 8 of 22 cases sit in a repeated
family; only 14 cases are the sole case of their family.
The bar in ROADMAP M1 is 20 MEALS = 20 distinct dishes. 17 < 20, so the bar is
NOT met, and any score quoted from this corpus must carry BOTH numbers.
Per-batch, the same way: batch 1 = 7 cases / 7 families; batch 2 (median 15.4%)
Producer: tools/ai_accuracy.py --corpus, which is the ONE definition of a
family; test/corpus_independence_test.dart executes it rather than re-deriving
it, and fails if these declared numbers stop matching the file.
"17 distinct families": 17 was the count of distinct dish NAMES at 22 cases.
Grouped by the judgement a scan actually has to make, that corpus was 13
distinct dish CLASSES - Dal / Dal Makhani / Urad Dal are one class,
Chole / Chana Masala one, Palak Paneer / Matar Paneer one, mutton / chicken /
dum biryani one - and dal, chole and sambar alone held 14 of its 22 cases.
BATCH 5 CLOSED PART OF THE GAP, from free photos and no model budget:
27 cases / 22 distinct dish names / 18 distinct dish CLASSES / 33 coverage
classes. New classes: khichdi, biryani, sarson da saag, aloo gobi, kofta.
The bar is 20 MEALS, so 18 of 20 - two classes short, from 13.
A third number, printed so the conservative one cannot be picked for me:
COVERAGE = 26 distinct classes across EVERY labelled item, because a thali holds
four judgements and class_of() only sees the first non-staple one.
22 cases / 17 names / 13 case-level classes / 26 coverage classes. The harness
prints all four and says which one the bar is judged on.
BATCH 5 (2026-09-28): 24 candidates fetched, 6 looked at, 5 ACCEPTED and
13 rejected with the reason recorded in photos.json. The batch was built
from the gap, not from what was easy: BATCH5_QUERIES is one query per
dish class the corpus lacked, and the fetcher grew a near-duplicate
check (64-bit dHash, Hamming <= 8) plus per-query and per-author caps
BEFORE fetching, because the fish-curry query offered five near-identical
files by one uploader. New classes: khichdi, biryani, sarson da saag,
aloo gobi, kofta. Two candidates were rejected for a truth I could not
name honestly, which is the rule working, not the rule being awkward.
BATCH 6 (2026-09-28): the last two classes the bar needed, chosen by GAP not
by convenience - one non-vegetarian class in 27 cases, no egg, no dessert,
no rice dish. BATCH6_QUERIES is one query per missing class. 8 candidates
fetched, 5 looked at, 3 ACCEPTED and 4 rejected with reasons, 1 declared
not-used because nobody looked at it.
NEW CLASSES: egg (egg bhurji), pulao (veg pulao + boondi raitha), kheer.
MEASURED: 30 cases / 25 distinct dish names / 21 distinct dish CLASSES / 35
coverage classes. The bar is 20 MEALS, so it is MET with one class spare,
and it is met honestly: egg bhurji and omelette are one class, mutton and
chicken biryani are one class, so a batch cannot buy the bar with synonyms.
BATCH 7 (2026-09-28): the SKEW, not the count. 13 of 30 cases were four
classes (dal x5, chole x4, paneer x2, sambar x2) = 43% of the corpus, so a
median over it is largely a median over dal and chole. Five classes were
targeted; Commons returned one usable photograph.
accepted 1  gajar halwa (a second dessert class; kheer was the only one)
rejected 3  a styled Bengali banana-leaf fish thali with three
unnameable items, an unidentifiable pale protein curry, and
a sweets-shop shot that repeats the halwa class
not_used 1  fetched, never looked at
So 21 -> 22 classes and the skew barely moved. Reported as it is: I am not
inflating a batch by accepting photographs I cannot label. The skew guard
pins the CURRENT concentration so it cannot worsen, and names <= 35% as the
target for a future batch instead of pretending it has been reached.
SKEW: 13 of 31 cases are four classes (dal x5, chole x4, paneer x2, sambar x2) = 42%. The bar is met, the SAMPLE is not yet even, and both facts belong in every number quoted from this corpus.

cases.note: In-repo original: one katori palak paneer + one roti.
OUT OF SCOPE on purpose. Chickpeas, avocado, tomato, cucumber, greens. No Indian dish is present; any Indian answer here is an invention.
Steel tray, shot from above. Unambiguous: a large portion of white rice, a yellow dal, a dry green sabzi, a brown curry, one empty compartment.
One steel bowl of dal makhani, near-overhead, cream streaks and cream visible. The single most identifiable Indian dish there is.
A white bowl of yellow kadhi seen from above, with a ghee and red-chilli temper garnish. 'Medium' because a scan could reasonably call this dal.

A yellow bowl of urad dal with two chapati on a plate, with raw onion rings, cucumber and lemon on the side. BATCH-1 CORRECTION: the first run scored onion and cucumber as INVENTED dishes. They are plainly in the photo - I described them in the note and then forgot to put them in the truth. The harness was right; my label was wrong.

Steel plate, overhead. A bowl of chole (chickpeas in gravy with green chilli), a dry spiced potato bhaji, two chapati, and a glass of tea. BATCH-1 CORRECTION: the first label said 'Chole, Dal, Roti' - there is NO dal in this photo, and the reference total was 200 kcal short, which is what produced the alarming 37.7% error. The model was closer to right than my label was. Corrected after looking at the image at full size.
White oval plate from above: a mound of white rice and bhindi masala (okra in a red gravy, coriander and green chilli).
One white plate, overhead: a mound of roasted mashed eggplant with visible seeds and green chilli. A single dish.
A steel bowl on a plain blue background, shot from above: pale green bottle-gourd cubes in a thin yellow-brown gravy.

A yellow bowl of matar paneer (paneer strips and green peas in an orange-red gravy). Loose peas and a block of paneer sit beside the bowl as styling, and are NOT labelled - a person photographing their lunch would log the bowl. That choice is why this case is 'medium'.

A square plate: two chapati, a chopped green bhindi sabzi and a yellow dal. NOTE: the file is named '...and_dal_rice' but there is NO rice in the photo - I labelled from the image, not the filename. There is also a small dark item at the plate edge I cannot identify, so it is left unlabelled rather than guessed.

A folded masala dosa on a steel plate with two small bowls of chutney, shot from above. 'Medium' because the filling inside the fold is not visible, so the potato-vs-onion split is a judgement call, and the two chutneys cannot be told apart.
A white plate from above: four steamed idli and two small bowls, one pale brown and one orange. Home-style, not styled.
Rava idli in a steel bowl on a home table, with sambar in a black bowl and two chutney bowls. Overhead and plainly home-cooked.

A single uthappam on a banana leaf with small bowls of sambar and chutney. Unmistakable and clearly a home serving. CORRECTION 2026-09-28: this case was previously reported as the worst failure - the model 'inventing' a dish. Measured live, the model answered "Vegetable Uttapam", which IS this dish; my alias list simply lacked that spelling. The model was right and my label was the bug. A false accusation is worse than no measurement because it sends you fixing the wrong thing.
On a banana leaf: two idli, one golden vada, a bowl of sambar and chutney, with a steel tumbler. 'Medium' because vada and boondi in the sambar can be confused at this size.
A white plate from above: chole in a small steel bowl with two papad triangles beside it. Clean, home-style, plainly identifiable.
A close overhead view of chana masala cooking in a pan, garnished with coriander. 'Medium' because there is no plate or bowl for scale, so the portion is an estimate.
A steel thali from above: chole, a puri, and a portion of gajar halwa. Three clearly separate items.
A white plate from above: kidney beans with brinjal pieces in a brown masala. 'Medium' because rajma-with-brinjal and plain rajma are a judgement call from the photo alone.

The corpus's only NON-VEGETARIAN case, which is a real gap: our users are not all vegetarian and nothing else tested that. The photographer's own Commons description is the ground truth here, and it lists MORE than I first labelled: 'plain rice, dal, rajma, fish with mustard, chicken curry, carrot and cucumber salad, pickle, green chili, papad, and kheer'. My first label named only four items, which would have scored real food as invented. Using the photographer's description rather than my eye, because on a crowded plate my eye is the weaker authority.

Gujarati khichuri on a steel-and-ceramic plate, from above: a bowl of khichdi, three khakra, one dry vegetable sabzi. The small steel katori of thin dal/sauce is NOT in the truth: I could not name it honestly, and a guess in the truth column is how an earlier baseline was wrong by 37.7%.

Home-cooked plate from above: a large plate of mutton biryani with mutton pieces and a whole potato, a small glass bowl of extra mutton gravy, and cucumber slices. The extra gravy bowl is counted inside the biryani figure, not as a second dish.
One steel bowl of sarson da saag and one makki di roti, shot from above. Countable, and the classic winter pairing - a dish class the corpus had no case for at all.
One white bowl of aloo gobi on a newspaper, close to above. A single-dish case, which the corpus barely had: most of its cases are thalis, so a one-bowl scan was never measured.
Twelve kofta in a red gravy on a square plate, from above. The count is deliberate: this is a COUNTING case as well as a naming one, and counting is where the app has been weakest.

A yellow compartment tray shot from above: egg bhurji with onion, tomato and coriander; three chapati; and a meat curry in two compartments. THE MEAT IS NOT IDENTIFIABLE from the photo, so the truth says 'Meat Curry' and every specific answer is an accepted alias - a model that says mutton when it is beef has not invented anything, and a truth column that demanded one answer would score it wrong for a reason that is not the model's fault. The 2nd meat compartment is counted once.

A white bowl of veg pulao on a floral plate beside a yellow bowl of boondi raitha, from above. The rice is WHITE, not yellow, so pulao vs plain rice with vegetables is a judgement - 'Rice' is therefore an accepted alias, and the label is medium confidence rather than a pretence of certainty.

One steel bowl of chahao kheer - purple rice pudding with milk - on a tablecloth, with a spoon. The corpus had NO dessert case at all, and a thali photograph routinely contains one: the only dessert in the corpus before this was gajar halwa, inside someone else's thali.

A glass bowl of gajar ka halwa with two cashews on top, on a blue plate, three tomato slices beside it, shot from above. One clearly readable dish plus a garnish - the shape of case the corpus barely had, and a second dessert class after kheer.
